Done. T4 solved on the first execution.

**Approach:** a direct script on `safetensors` (lazy `safe_open`, one tensor name at a time) + `torch`, at `out/T4/solution.py`, with `out/T4/run.sh` as the runner.

I skipped mergekit's `task_arithmetic` — the nominal condition-F route — because it applies its merge to every tensor rather than a verified subset, has no precondition check that the three checkpoints agree outside the trained tensors (which the task makes mandatory), and re-serializes to a sharded model, putting bit-exactness of the 66 untouched tensors and the single-file/114-tensor requirement at the mercy of its writer.

**Checks the run enforces**, each aborting non-zero: identical key sets across base/ft1/ft2; 114 tensors; the MLP pattern matching exactly 48 names; per-tensor shape/dtype agreement; every non-MLP tensor bit-identical in all three; exactly 48 tensors merged; and the written file re-opened and confirmed at 114 tensors with the base key set.

**Ordering hazard** handled by never mutating the running tensor: both task vectors are taken against the freshly-read `base[X]` in one expression. Untouched tensors are copied straight from the base with no arithmetic, so they stay bit-exact.

Independent verification after the write: exactly 48 tensors differ from the base, a spot-checked merged tensor matches the formula to 0.0 relative error in float32, and embeddings / attention / `lm_head` are bit-exact. Run took 13 s.
